subject: Post-call: HelioHealth cost & pilot action items
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heliohealth.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@heliohealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: HelioHealth cost & pilot action items

Hi Samira / Raj — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the action list so everyone has the same view. I’ve attached a short pilot proposal and a sample traffic schema we discussed.

Key pain points we heard
- Unit economics: peak token bill is a major constraint for production launch; current cost run-rate from your GA model is ~3x of internal budget targets.
- Bursty traffic: telemedicine batch jobs spike during mornings and evenings, and tail latency matters for patient-facing flows.
- Quality sensitivity: you can tolerate modest quality change for async jobs (summaries) but not for real-time transcripts/triage.

Current stack / constraints (as discussed)
- Serving today: hosted open model (variant A) through vendor X, CPU-backed autoscale, AWS us-west.
- Batch vs realtime split: ~60% realtime (p99 latency target 200–400ms), 40% async micro-batches.
- Regulatory: PHI in payloads for certain flows — will need SOC2 + VPC options for pilot progression.

Success criteria for pilot (proposed)
1) Demonstrate >=35% reduction in token inference cost for async workloads via batching / cache improvements while keeping quality delta <= 3% on our eval prompts.
2) Realtime path: maintain p99 latency under 400ms with graceful degradation and fallbacks.
3) Security: pilot runs inside an isolated VPC with audit logs retained for 30 days.

Proposed immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Helio: share 48-hour sample traffic (anonymized) and mark which endpoints can tolerate quantized models — Samira by Mon 12/14.
- Redwood Eng (Marissa): run a quick profiling pass against sample traffic and return batching/caching recommendations — deliverable by Thu 12/17.
- Redwood Sales (Aditya): send pilot commercial outline (duration, minimal committed spend, optional SLA) — EOD Mon 12/14.
- Setup: exchange test credentials (temporary) + invite to a shared drive with pilot docs — Grace to own.

Attachments: pilot proposal, traffic schema, preliminary cost breakdown template. If you want, we can split the pilot: start async batching + quantization on non-critical flows first, then add realtime routing rules.

When works for a 30m follow-up to kick off pilot? I'm proposing Wed 12/16 10:00–10:30 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite unless you suggest another slot.

Thanks — Grace
--
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments referenced: redwood-pilot-proposal-helio.pdf (PDF), traffic-sample-schema.json (JSON), model_cost_breakdown.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heliohealth.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@heliohealth.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: HelioHealth cost & pilot action items

Thanks Grace — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Traffic sample: we'll provide an anonymized 72-hour export instead of 48 since it captures two morning peaks — delivering by EOD Tue 12/15. Will mark endpoints that are non-PII and those that carry PHI.

2) Quantization openness: engineering is open to trying 4-bit/INT4 for async summaries and non-clinical enrichment, but we need a clear rollback path if hallucinations or quality regressions show up. For realtime triage we’re conservative — prefer smaller model variants + faster routing over heavy quantization initially.

3) Procurement question: what does the minimal committed spend look like for a 4-week pilot that includes dedicated pool capacity? Also curious about billing cadence and any overage handling.

We’re aiming to make a decision on pilot go/no-go by Fri 12/18.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product, NLP | HelioHealth
samira.khan@heliohealth.ai | +1 (617) 555-9044
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heliohealth.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@heliohealth.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: HelioHealth cost & pilot action items

Appreciate the quick response, Samira. Short replies to procurement and quantization notes: 

- Pilot commercial: for a 4-week dedicated pilot (reserved pool during peak hours + shared capacity off-peak) we typically propose a fixed pilot fee that covers reserved GPU hours + reduced per-token overage. I'll draft ranges and a minimal commitment option (two tiers) and share by EOD Mon 12/14.

- Rollback and safety: engineering-run can keep an A/B split so your live traffic can automatically fallback to unquantized variant on detection of quality drop. We'll include automated evaluation hooks in the pilot.

Marissa — can your team prioritize a profiling pass once we have the anonymized sample? Grace — I’ll coordinate the pilot commercial and loop in finance for billing cadence options.

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com

Great — thanks everyone. Quick confirmation of owners & dates so we can keep momentum: 
- Helio (Samira): anonymized 72-hour traffic + PHI flags — Tue 12/15 EOD.
- Redwood Eng (Marissa): profiling + batching/caching recommendation — Thu 12/17 COB.
- Redwood Sales (Aditya): pilot commercial + two-tier minimal commitment options — Mon 12/14 EOD (sending now).
- Redwood (Grace): calendar invite for Wed 12/16 10:00 PT sent (please accept) + share drive link with attachments.

If anything slips, call it out in the thread so we can adjust the pilot start date. Looking forward to moving to a short pilot to quantify unit-econ improvements.

Cheers — Grace
